expectations.text: Proposes validating the METRIC itself against a case whose answer is already known (e.g. point mode, where it must be ~0)
expectations.evidence: §2b "Arithmetic self-tests -- PASSED": synthetic vectors with known parts (normal 5, along-path 13, cross-path 7, with a tangent deliberately not perpendicular to the normal) "recovers 5.000000 / 13.000000 / 7.000000 exactly", reconstructing to 1e-9. `_wpct` is checked against a hand-computable weighted-median case and against numpy at equal weights. §2e runs point mode (`--run 900`) as a known-answer case: f_max 23.925980963125905 "with all stroke fields zero".

expectations.text: Measures in the PAD frame rather than the TCP/wrist frame, or explains why the wrist frame would mislead
expectations.evidence: Implements `Cell._cmd_pad_pos()` and explains the frame trap explicitly: "you cannot read the pad geom out of the scratch data after `mj_kinematics` ... FK on a copied qpos leaves the pad exactly where it already was, so the metric would read ~0 mm no matter how far the arm lagged." Instead it takes "the pad's measured offset in the live TCP frame and re-apply[ies] it to the commanded TCP frame ... leaving exactly the wrist's pose error mapped out to the pad."

expectations.text: Handles teleports: uses velocity state or otherwise avoids raw position differencing across discontinuities
expectations.evidence: The error vector is an instantaneous same-step difference between the measured pad position and the commanded pad position derived by FK on `q_des`; no differencing of positions across time steps occurs, so a mid-cycle teleport cannot enter the number. §2c adds a non-degeneracy guard against the related free-body failure ("Not zero (which would mean the free-body trap)"). Caveat: teleports/discontinuities are never named as a hazard.

expectations.text: Decomposes the error into in-plane (coverage) vs surface-normal (flange compression) rather than reporting one mixed number
expectations.evidence: Three-way decomposition table -- normal ("the active contact flange compressing ... No [not an error]"), along-path lag ("No -- the pad sweeps the same ground, later"), cross-path ("Yes -- this is the headline servo number") -- with the tangent orthogonalised against the normal "otherwise flange travel leaks into the lag term". §3 shows the undecomposed version was caught and rejected: "The 18.46 mm I would have shipped as 'servo tracking error' was 86% an artefact of my own frame choice."
